source_record: Live DB: Ezekiel 27:32 word_id 238432, pointed בְּנִיהֶם֙, Strong's H5204, morphology HR/Ncmsc/Sp3mp. No local textual qere row is attached to this word.
independent_evidence: BDB H5204 marks the MT lexical reading as doubtful and reports בְּנֵיהֶם ('their sons') in 11 MSS, early editions, LXX, Arabic, Theodotion, and Syriac. The Greek LXX text displayed for Ezekiel 27:32 reads καὶ λήμψονται οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτῶν ἐπὶ σὲ θρῆνον ('and their sons will take up a lament for you'), aligning with 'their sons'. Local word_variants for word_id 238432 has no qere row. YLT DB check: verse has 30 whitespace tokens but only 14 aligned positions; word_id 238432 is bridged to YLT positions 1 'And' and 2 'lifted', while word_id 238430 (וְנָשְׂאוּ, H5375) has no mapping and positions 7 'their' / 8 'sons' are unaligned.
assessment: A genuine textual/lexical ambiguity under the same consonantal spelling: MT בְּנִיהֶם is parsed as 'in their wailing'; multiple witnesses and LXX support בְּנֵיהֶם ('their sons'). Keep the MT token and external-witness reading separate. This is not a Masoretic qere unless the source apparatus explicitly says so. The existing YLT alignment is also a strong U-1 anomaly: it appears to map the MT H5204 word to 'And/lifted' while leaving the YLT 'their sons' phrase unaligned. This does not authorize changes to the translation or alignment.
next_action: Preserve MT and LXX readings separately. If YLT alignment work resumes, review the 14/30 mapped positions in this verse as a separate U-1 task; do not recompute or rewrite alignments during this Hebrew variant review.

references: Numbers 13:21; 34:8 (also batch groups with Genesis 48:7 and Jeremiah 42:15)
source_record: Live DB: Numbers 13:21 word_id 47351, pointed לְבֹ֥א, H935, morphology HNp; Numbers 34:8 word_id 55394, pointed לְבֹ֣א, H935, morphology HNp. The project's pinned OSHB source commit is 3d15126fb1ef74867fc1434be1942e837932691f.
independent_evidence: WLC transcriptions in Numbers 13:21 and 34:8 contain לְבֹא. Independent WLC analysis assigns H935 and labels it a verb/“entering”; UBS Handbook on Numbers reports both “entrance of Hamath” and the toponym “Lebo-hamath,” recommending the toponym rendering for Num 13:21 based on 1 Kgs 8:65 while noting “Hamath Pass” as plausible. The Num 34:8 commentary uses “entrance of Hamath.” Project parser parse_oshb.py copies XML @morph verbatim to TSV; README confirms this. Therefore HNp is likely inherited from the pinned OSHB XML, though exact token attributes have not yet been directly retrieved.
assessment: The token's verbal/infinitive analysis is supported by independent morphology, but phrase-level interpretation as an entrance/pass or a place-name remains disputed in scholarly translation resources. The project's HNp annotation is not disproved by the infinitive analysis alone; keep both token morphology and phrase-boundary interpretation open.
next_action: Inspect the exact pinned OSHB XML lemma/morph attributes for both word IDs and compare the source's mapping to the database. Keep the place-name/entrance interpretation open; no source correction yet.
